query: What travel policy risks appear in expense descriptions?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Categorises the asset/CI into meaningful types, with a 'travel_equipment' bucket directly relevant to the travel-policy query. Values (hardware_device from Dell laptops, service from AWS) are well grounded in the CI text. Only moderately useful since it is asset-centric rather than policy-risk-centric, but it gives a genuine grouping axis.

per_column.name: travel_purpose_indicator
per_column.rationale: Directly on-target for the query: separates travel_related vs office_based vs service. Samples are reasonable readings (hardware->office_based, cloud service->service_based). Groundedness slightly reduced because the travel/office split leans on inference from terse descriptions, but the readings shown are defensible.

per_column.name: business_legitimacy_clarity
per_column.rationale: Highly relevant axis for policy-risk analysis (personal_travel_signal, ambiguous_business_purpose). However 124 'personal_travel_signal' labels are hard to justify from source texts that are largely generic asset/hardware procurement descriptions; the shown samples are all 'clear_business_purpose' from neutral text, so the personal-signal assignments risk asserting intent the text does not support.

per_column.name: high_value_asset_flag
per_column.rationale: A near 50/50 boolean split is weakly informative and only loosely tied to the travel-policy query. Groundedness is questionable: an AWS EC2 instance is flagged high_value=True while Dell laptops are False, and the source rows shown contain no price/amount cues to justify a specific value threshold, suggesting the flag is inferred beyond available evidence.

per_column.name: processing_delay_flag
per_column.rationale: Delay could be computed from opened_at vs processed_date, so values are potentially grounded, but the column is largely orthogonal to travel-policy risk. Adds little analytical leverage for THIS query.

per_column.name: ci_asset_specificity
per_column.rationale: Well grounded (branded_model for 'Dell Latitude 3410', service_name for AWS). But it describes naming specificity of the CI, largely redundant with asset_category_type and only tangentially useful for detecting travel-policy risk.

per_column.name: creation_method
per_column.rationale: Grounded in the description wording ('Automated creation' -> automated_generation, 'Procurement' -> manual_procurement). However it captures record provenance, not travel-policy risk, so it offers little leverage for the query.

judge.rationale: Two or three columns (travel_purpose_indicator, business_legitimacy_clarity, and to a lesser extent asset_category_type) directly serve the travel-policy-risk query and provide genuine grouping axes. The remainder (high_value_asset_flag, processing_delay_flag, ci_asset_specificity, creation_method) are either boolean/near-generic, redundant, or oriented toward asset/record metadata rather than travel policy, dragging holistic usefulness to mid-range. Groundedness is generally acceptable and most values are sound readings of the CI/description text, but the intent-laden labels (personal_travel_signal, high_value flag) assert specifics not clearly supported by the terse source rows shown, warranting the moderate groundedness score.
